newsitem.title: CHINA: Yuan down slightly against US dollar in Shanghai.
newsitem.headline: Yuan down slightly against US dollar in Shanghai.

text.p: The Chinese yuan closed slightly lower against the U.S. dollar at 8.2947 in Shanghai on Monday, down from last Friday's 8.2945.
The yuan opened lower at 8.2948 and fluctuated around 8.2950 for most of the session, hitting an intraday low of 8.2951 and a sudden high of 8.2850 during midsession.
Trading was slow with most done at 8.2947, traders said.
Although the yuan was lowered by profit-taking late in trading, strong pro-yuan sentiment boosted the currency to close above 8.2950, traders said.
One dealer said that active bids were seen below the 8.2950 level, a point of resistance breached last Friday.
"Limited central bank intervention also allowed the yuan to rise," he said.
With no new factors affecting the yuan market, its main stimulus was demand for the currency before the Chinese lunar new year holiday, beginning on February 6, a second dealer said.
"The yuan will consolidate slowly upward before the holiday," he said.
Dealers expected the yuan to move above 8.2950 on Tuesday.
The yuan closed slightly up at 6.9500 from 6.9600 against 100 Japanese yen and little changed at 1.0715 from 1.0714 against the Hong Kong dollar.
